topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students to the final lecture and outlines the core learning objectives regarding cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical mechanisms, adverse toxicities, and resistance pathways associated with conventional cancer treatments.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities and defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic approaches designed to selectively exploit intrinsic genetic and molecular vulnerabilities in cancer cells.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic drivers and kinase inhibitor resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the targeted inhibition of hyperactive oncogenic kinases and the molecular mechanisms underlying therapy resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody and antibody-drug conjugate therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the therapeutic application of engineered monoclonal antibodies to target tumor cells directly and to deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: T-cell-mediated anti-tumor immunity and immunotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the role of host anti-tumor immunity and the development of strategies that reactivate or genetically engineer T cells to eliminate tumors.

topics.label: Progress, challenges, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the broader clinical progress, persistent biological challenges, and future ethical and therapeutic directions in oncology.
